_comment: LIVE — panes of the RUNNING app he can hover, click and drag, answered Yes / No or pick one.

This is the right shape for motion, drag, hover and resize: a 200 ms animation cannot be judged from a recording. Each pane boots its own copy of the app from one authored candidate in youcoded's compare/registry.tsx, so build that first.
No pictures at all, so this deck names no images folder and no runs. serve boots the workbench of the worktree below; four panes is the cap, because each one is a whole app.
title: Switching sessions — try it
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His answers are saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_themes: themes: the palette the panes boot in. He can switch it on the page.

live._comment: live (deck level): which build the panes come from. Required — every candidate in one review has to come from one build, or he is comparing two different apps.
live._comment_worktree: worktree: the name of the worktree whose workbench serve boots. It must hold the candidates named below.
live._comment_paneWidth: paneWidth (optional): how wide the registry says this surface is. Only for laying the row out; over 1600 the page warns, because one pane wider than a screen scrolls sideways.

steps._comment: A TRY-THIS step: one pane, answered Yes / No. Same words as an approve step — the pane is just a live picture.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this point. It labels his answer.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The row of sessions along the top
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there.
steps.headline: Drag a session sideways — do the others get out of the way soon enough?
steps._comment_headline: headline: the one sentence he reads first, and the thing to DO. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.changed: The sessions beside the one you drag step aside while you move, instead of jumping when you let go.
steps._comment_changed: changed: the What changed card. One or two sentences.
steps._comment_measured: measured: the timing you are asking about.
steps.notice: You can see where the session will land before you drop it.
steps._comment_notice: notice: the You'll notice card. What to watch for while he plays with it.
steps.risk: Dragging fast over several neighbours puts a lot of motion on screen at once.

live._comment: live (step level): the address of the design this pane shows.
live._comment_surface: surface: the surface's name in the compare registry.
live._comment_round: round: which round of that surface. REQUIRED — candidate names repeat across rounds, so an address without one silently shows an older design.
live._comment_candidate: candidate: which authored design, for a one-pane step. On a pick-one step this moves onto each variant instead.

steps._comment: A PICK-ONE step: two to four panes side by side, and he picks one. Same shape as a choice step, with running panes instead of pictures.
steps.headline: How should the conversation arrive when you switch to it?
steps.risk: Only the whole view moves, so a long conversation costs no more than a short one.

variants._comment: One pane. It boots the app on this candidate; he drives it himself.
variants._comment_id: id: your name for this design. It is what his answer records.
variants.label: Fade and lift
variants._comment_label: label: the design's name, two or three words.
variants._comment_candidate: candidate: this design's name in the registry, under the surface and round above.
variants.summary: Fades in while rising a little. The quietest of the two.
variants._comment_summary: summary: one or two sentences on what this design is.
variants._comment_measured: measured (optional): the timing. Needs a digit in it.
variants.risk: On a slow machine the fade can look like a delay.
variants._comment_risk: risk (optional): what is wrong with THIS design in particular.

variants.label: Spring up
variants.summary: Rises further and overshoots a touch before settling.
